item.title: CBS News Battleground Tracker poll: Democrats hold edge in bid for House control
item.description: Price concerns boost Democrats, and MAGA Republicans are motivated. Both parties are seen negatively, according to CBS News' latest polling.

item.title: CBS News political panel on what voters can expect to see on the midterm campaign trail
item.description: With the midterm elections less than two months away, CBS News executive director of elections and surveys Anthony Salvanto, CBS News senior White House and political correspondent Ed O'Keefe and Amy Walter, editor-in-chief of Cook Political Report, join to discuss what voters can expect to see on the midterm campaign trail and the outlook for both parties.

item.title: Utah Gov. Spencer Cox says government needs to "protect the public" on AI
item.description: Utah's Republican Gov. Spencer Cox told "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" that the government needs to come together to "protect the public" on AI, saying "government doesn't get this right often either, but we should be at the table working together, and that's what we've done in Utah."

item.title: CBS Battleground Tracker poll: Democrats hold edge in bid for House control
item.description: The CBS News Battleground Tracker poll finds that both Republicans and Democrats see the midterms as being about President Trump, albeit for different reasons. CBS News executive director of elections and surveys Anthony Salvanto joined "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" to delve deeper into the poll's findings.

item.title: Face the Nation: Cox, Salvanto, political panel
item.description: Missed the second half of the show? Utah Gov. Spencer Cox, CBS News executive director of elections and surveys Anthony Salvanto and our political panel with Salvanto, CBS news senior White House and political correspondent Ed O'Keefe and Amy Walter, editor-in-chief and publisher of the Cook Political Report.

item.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says U.S.-China AI race poses "toughest dilemma"
item.description: In an exclusive interview with CBS News' Jo Ling Kent, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called on the tech industry to slow the development of AI. But, he acknowledged the "toughest dilemma" is coming to an international agreement amid the development race between the U.S.and China.

item.title: Admiral Brad Cooper says he's "not concerned at all" about munition shortage
item.description: "60 Minutes" correspondent Norah O'Donnell spoke to Admiral Brad Cooper, the commander in charge of the war in Iran. He told O'Donnell "I'm not concerned at all" about a munitions shortage to defend against Iranian missile and drone attacks. Watch the full interview on "60 Minutes" on CBS or Paramount+ this Sunday, Sept. 13 at 7:30 p.m. ET.

item.title: Uncovering a Holocaust survival story
item.description: A school oral history project to interview World War II veterans uncovered little-known stories from the conflict, including the liberation by American troops of 2,500 Holocaust survivors from a so-called "death train" in April 1945.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Sept. 13)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed says public oversight needed on AI to avoid serving "interests of a few"
item.description: Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed told "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" that a public agency needs be developed focused on AI, saying that "we collectively have to decide that we need public oversight so that all of this technology is not being created for the interests of a few against the well-being of many."

item.title: Wisconsin Congressman suffers minor injury after lake emergency landing
item.description: The congressman thanked the pilot and first responders for coming to their aid, and expressed his gratitude at only having sustained minor injuries.

item.description: Once shunned over its extremist roots, the Sweden Democrats could enter government for the first time as voters weigh immigration, crime and Sweden's political transformation.

item.title: Diane von Furstenberg on life, love, and a wrap dress
item.description: One of the most important names in fashion for nearly 50 years, Diane von Furstenberg has long empowered women, with practical, feminine clothing, most famously embodied by her '70s wrap dress.

item.description: The Iran-backed Houthis expanded their control over the strategy Bab-el-Mandeb strait, as strikes continued in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Loopholes and shady practices taint U.S. surrogacy industry
item.description: Lured by promises of payment and a desire to help other families, surrogates discover they have few protections from practices that cast a "dark shadow" over the industry.

item.title: Nature: Monarch caterpillars in New York
item.description: We leave you this Sunday morning with hungry monarch caterpillars, munching away in New York's Hudson Valley. Videographer: Lorraine Mullins.

item.title: Good gourd! A visit to the pumpkin capital of the world
item.description: In Morton, Illinois, home to the annual Pumpkin Festival, and site of the Libby's factory responsible for 85 percent of the world's canned pumpkin, correspondent Nancy Giles gets a taste of the local produce and finds out why, in Morton, orange is always in season.

item.title: Testing the ethical boundaries of surrogacy
item.description: In the United States, commercial surrogacy — paying a woman to have fertilized eggs implanted in her uterus so she can carry a pregnancy to term — is widely assumed to be closely regulated. But a yearlong CBS News investigation found that few, if any, meaningful protections exist for surrogates. Correspondent Katrina Kaufman examines the extraordinary cases of surrogates who say they experienced troubling practices in the booming U.S. industry.

item.title: Extended interview: Diane von Furstenberg
item.description: In this web exclusive, fashion designer Diane von Furstenberg talks with correspondent Alina Cho about the origin and legacy of the wrap dress; aging; and the lessons she learned from her mother, a Holocaust survivor. She also discusses her annual DVF Awards (now in its 17th year), which celebrate women of accomplishment.

item.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei: "For too long the industry lied" about AI risks
item.description: The head of the artificial intelligence company calls the exponential rate of AI developments a "warning sign," with risks for humanity, and says, "We need to slow down." He talks with "Sunday Morning" about possible steps forward.

item.title: 9/13: Sunday Morning
item.description: Hosted by Jane Pauley. Featured: America's missile arsenal; Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on the development of AI; fashion designer Diane von Furstenberg; testing the ethical boundaries of surrogacy; uncovering a Holocaust survival story; the allure of shipwrecks; and the annual Pumpkin Festival in Morton, Ill.

item.title: Pope Leo commemorates 9/11 attacks, calls for renewed commitment to peace
item.description: The Chicago-born pope​ made his first public comments to commemorate 25 years since the attacks, speaking in English at the end of his traditional Sunday noon blessing.

item.title: Cardiac event reveals Olympian's rare heart condition: "There was a God present"
item.description: Olympian Jenny Simpson said she won't be able to run again after being diagnosed with a rare heart condition earlier this year.
